raw.details:
AI coding agents are powerful until they hit the same build, dependency, or runtime error for the third session in a row and burn tokens re-debugging it from scratch.

CoMemor is a fast-growing, local-first Model Context Protocol (MCP) server (npx comemor, freshly launched v1.1.0) that equips AI coding agents including Cursor, Claude Desktop & Code, VS Code + Copilot, Windsurf, and Google Antigravity with deterministic, repository-scoped engineering memory powered by SHA-256 error fingerprinting, SQLite FTS5 lexical search, automated secret redaction, and prompt-injection quarantine.

The CoMemor Contributor Challenge invites developers, AI builders, and open-source enthusiasts to ship real production code, sharpen our security and retrieval engine, hunt edge-case bugs, and showcase their engineering work in public. Top contributors earn official certificates and a direct shot at an internship opportunity with the CoMemor team.

Contribution Tracks (Pick Any or Multiple)

  • Core MCP Engine & Retrieval: Improve TypeScript modules, SQLite FTS5 ranking, error normalization and find_fix / record_failure / verify_fix edge cases.
  • Security, Hardening & Testing: Strengthen secret-redaction patterns, prompt-injection heuristics, Vitest unit/integration tests, and retrieval benchmarks.
  • Memory Console & Developer Experience: Enhance the local Memory Console UI, IDE setup workflows, cross-platform Windows/macOS/Linux compatibility, and documentation.
  • High-Signal Bug Hunting & RFCs: Identify reproducible bugs, security edge cases, or well-scoped architectural feature proposals via GitHub Issues.

How to Participate (Step-by-Step)

  • Register on Unstop: Complete your individual registration before the deadline.
  • Connect with the Project:
    • Star and Watch the CoMemor GitHub repository to track open issues and releases.
  • Pick or Propose Work: Browse issues labeled good first issue, help wanted, or contributor-challenge or open a clear, reproducible new issue before coding.
  • Ship Quality Contributions: Fork the repo, follow Contributing.md, ensure tests pass locally, and open a well-documented Pull Request.
  • Showcase Your Work on LinkedIn (Required for Leaderboard Scoring): After submitting your PR or verified issue, publish a short video demo (30–90 seconds) or a concise technical article/post on LinkedIn explaining the problem you solved and what you added or fixed in CoMemor. Tag the CoMemor LinkedIn page and include the hashtags #comemor, #comemorcontributor, #opensource, and #mcp.
  • Submit Proof on Unstop: Submit your GitHub username, PR/Issue links, and LinkedIn post link during the submission window.

Format & Rounds

  • Round 1: Registration & Repo Onboarding: Register on Unstop, star & watch the repository, follow CoMemor on LinkedIn, set up the project locally and claim or open your first issue.
  • Round 2: Contribution & Build-in-Public Sprint: Submit Pull Requests and/or high-impact issues, respond to maintainer reviews, and publish your LinkedIn demo video or walkthrough post.
  • Round 3: Maintainer Review & Results: Final scoring of merged/accepted contributions, leaderboard announcement, certificate distribution, and internship interview invites for top contributors.

Guidelines & Eligibility

  • Eligibility: Open to college students, freshers, and working professionals from all branches and specializations.
  • Participation Format: Individual participation only (inter-college / open to all institutions).
  • Number of Contributions: Unlimited, you may submit multiple PRs or issues, and every merged/accepted contribution counts toward your final rank.

Rules & Quality Standards

  • All code and write-ups must be your original work and comply with CoMemor's GPL-3.0 license and CONTRIBUTING.md.
  • Use of AI is allowed and it is recommended to mention the specific AI Model or tool used for development.
  • Pull Requests must pass repository build and automated test checks (CI) and address a real bug, test gap, feature, or substantive docs improvement.
  • Zero Spam Policy: Low-effort PRs (trivial typo/whitespace edits, duplicate issues, or unverified AI-generated code dumps) will be closed and disqualified from certification.
  • You must comment on an issue to claim it before opening a PR if someone else is not already assigned.
  • Maintainer review and merge decisions are final.

Evaluation Criteria

  • Technical Depth & Code/Issue Quality (45%): Clean architecture, correctness, and real impact on CoMemor users.
  • Testing & Engineering Hygiene (25%): Test coverage, clear PR descriptions, adherence to repo conventions, and zero regressions.
  • LinkedIn Demo / Walkthrough Clarity (20%): Clear explanation of why the fix/feature matters and how it works in practice.
  • Collaboration & Review Responsiveness (10%): Constructive communication and timely iteration on maintainer feedback.

Rewards & Perks

  • Top Contributors: Chance to land an Internship Opportunity with the CoMemor team (shortlisted top performers invited for a direct technical conversation with the founder), Certificate of excellence, and a featured contributor spotlight on CoMemor's LinkedIn page and release notes.
  • Verified Contributors (All Merged PRs / Accepted High-Impact Issues + LinkedIn Demo): Official Verified Open-Source Contributor Certificate and permanent credit in CoMemor's GitHub release history.
